original_question: Which recessive mutation in a gene that catalyzes the NAD(P)H-dependent conversion of pyrroline-5-carboxylate to proline causes conditions very similar to those of De Barsy syndrome?

final_qi.question: Which recessive mutation in a gene that catalyzes the NAD(P)H-dependent conversion of pyrroline-5-carboxylate to proline causes conditions very similar to those of De Barsy syndrome?
final_qi.long_answer: Autosomal-recessive loss-of-function mutations in the PYCR1 gene, which encodes the mitochondrial NAD(P)H-dependent Δ¹-pyrroline-5-carboxylate reductase that converts pyrroline-5-carboxylate to proline, produce a cutis laxa/progeroid phenotype (ARCL2B) that is clinically very similar to De Barsy syndrome.

final_answer.long_answer: Autosomal-recessive loss-of-function mutations in the PYCR1 gene, which encodes the NAD(P)H-dependent pyrroline-5-carboxylate reductase-1 that converts pyrroline-5-carboxylate to proline, produce a progeroid form of autosomal recessive cutis laxa (ARCL2B). This condition shows the same key clinical features—cutis laxa, growth and developmental delay, and progeroid facial appearance—as the classic De Barsy syndrome, making the two disorders phenotypically very similar.
